text:
Washington led twice and still lost, because Carolina spent two periods taking the game away from them. WSH out-chanced CAR 1.79 to 0.66 in expected goals in the first period, and Boone Jenner's snap shot made it 1-0 at 9:26. After that the Capitals' share of the play collapsed. CAR held a 1.48 to 0.45 edge in the second and 2.05 to 0.47 in the third, and the scoreboard caught up with it.

The middle period swung on small things. Andrei Svechnikov tied it at 3:58, Justin Holl put WSH back ahead on an 8% chance at 6:39, and Eric Robinson tied it again at 18:49 on a 5% look, the least likely goal of the night. In the third, Svechnikov scored on the power play at 13:56 for a 3-2 lead. Mark Jankowski then finished it at 18:33 on an 86% chance, set up by Svechnikov and Sebastian Aho. Svechnikov finished with two goals and an assist, and CAR outscored WSH 3-0 over the last two periods.

Over the full game, CAR's 4.19 expected goals to WSH's 2.71 gave it a 60% chance of winning a replay of every shot, and the 77 to 47 edge in shot attempts shows the territorial gap. Pyotr Kochetkov stopped 20 of 22 shots against 2.71 expected goals against. Logan Thompson saved 31 of 34 for WSH, against 3.33 expected, so neither goalie bailed out his team. WSH had beaten CAR 5-2 on Oct. 2, but this time the better chances came from Carolina.
